correctness.rationale: For uniform admissible N-prefixes of X={x in {0,1}^N: x_j x_(2j)=0}, unique dyadic decomposition j=2^r i with odd i splits configurations into independent length L_i(N)=1+floor(log2(N/i)) golden-mean chains. Chain log-PF recurrence Z0=1,Z1=1+exp(t),Zk=Z(k-1)+exp(t) Z(k-2) yields exact first two moments. Since d_k(N)=N/2^(k+1)+O(1), convergent series define alpha~0.366541662066731 and sigma²~0.148936034454920>1/16, with mean alpha N+O(log²N), variance sigma² N+O(log³N). Independent-chain triangular-array Lindeberg, with max chain length O(log N), establishes the asserted normal law. Perron–Frobenius ratios give fixed-cylinder local Markov limit with initial (1/phi,1/phi²) and transition [[phi^-1,phi^-2],[1,0]]; its almost-sure digit density beta=2/(4+sqrt5)~0.320714913 follows q_(r+1)=phi^-2(1-q_r) and independent-chain Hoeffding. The bound sum_i L_i²<=6N yields TV>=1−4exp(−(alpha−beta)² N/48) for sufficiently large N, proving local and bulk separation. Independently enumerated legal words N=5,10,14 (20,288,2880 words) and checked series and moment recurrences. Finite cases are corroboration, not CLT/TV proof.
